messages:
Eli (customer): Hey team — since yesterday a subset of our users keep getting bounced to MFA immediately after SSO. They complete Okta MFA, get redirected back, then the app immediately shows the reauth modal again. Happens across Chrome and iOS app. Started after we toggled the new device-trust rollout.

Maya (support): Sorry you're hitting this — rough. Can you share repro steps and a couple of request/response headers from the browser console (or the mobile network trace)? Also which user ids affected and whether they see any error text in the UI?

Eli (customer): Steps: 1) Login via Okta SSO -> choose device and complete MFA 2) Okta posts to /auth/callback -> redirect to /app 3) UI loads, then 401 and opens MFA modal. Affected users: ~15% on same org. No UI error aside from "Session expired, please reauthenticate". Attaching headers:

```
POST /auth/callback HTTP/1.1
Host: app.redwood.ai
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
Cookie: rwd_session=; rwd_device=;

Response from auth:
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Set-Cookie: rwd_session=eyJ...; Path=/; Domain=.redwood.ai; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=3600
Set-Cookie: rwd_device=dt_abc123; Path=/; Domain=.redwood.ai; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=1209600
Location: https://app.redwood.ai/app
```

Eli (customer): Notice that the cookies are set but the browser shows Cookie header empty on the redirected /app GET (cookie not sent). This only happens when login originates from Okta (cross-site POST).

Maya (support): That crawl matches a SameSite cross-site set-cookie problem. When auth response is a cross-site POST from Okta, SameSite=Lax will block cookies on the subsequent navigation in some flows. Can you confirm whether Okta is doing a 302 redirect after POST vs returning a 200+script?

Eli (customer): Okta posts then issues a 302 back to app. We tested in Chrome dev tools — if I manually change SameSite=None it works consistently.

Kevin (eng-auth): Quick context from the auth service: we introduced a device-stamp rotation on login to improve device trust freshness. The device_jwt is minted with device_stamp X, and we set rwd_device cookie to match. Logs for one flow (trace id 0a3f):

```
[2026-03-15T14:12:07Z] INFO auth.callback trace=0a3f user=u_123 okta callback received
[2026-03-15T14:12:07Z] INFO auth.session create session_id=sess_55 ttl=3600 device_stamp=dt_abc123
[2026-03-15T14:12:07Z] WARN auth.session device-trust mismatch user=u_123 cookie_device=dt_old token_device=dt_abc123
[2026-03-15T14:12:07Z] ERROR auth.handler invalid_session: device_trust_mismatch
```

Kevin (eng-auth): Two immediate notes: (1) SameSite=Lax -> cross-site POST then 302 can sometimes drop cookies during the navigational GET, so your manual test matches. (2) We also rotated device_stamp in the token path unexpectedly in the rollout which made cookie_device!=token_device on first app load for some flows. Both together cause the quick reauth loop.

Sophie (eng-sre): Repro on staging would help. @Kevin can we enable auth.debug_session for this org so we capture device_stamp values + raw set-cookie headers? I can flip a debug flag on the canary.

Maya (support): Eli, can you confirm you consent to us enabling verbose debug in your org's staging-like tenant? We'll only capture transient headers and trace ids, no user PII.

Eli (customer): Yes please. Happy to help. We're fine with ephemeral debug for a few hours.

AuthBot: debug.feature.toggle auth.debug_session=1 for org=org_789 enabled on canary. (deployed to canary in 3m) :rocket:

Kevin (eng-auth): Suggested immediate mitigation for affected orgs: set rwd_session and rwd_device SameSite=None; Secure; make rwd_device persistent for at least 24h and align refresh_token.ttl with cookie TTL. Quick patch diff:

```
- Set-Cookie: rwd_session=...; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=3600
+ Set-Cookie: rwd_session=...; SameSite=None; Secure; Max-Age=3600
```

Kevin (eng-auth): Longer term we should: (a) avoid rotating device_stamp on the initial callback — only rotate on explicit device re-enroll; (b) add a small tolerant check for cookie missing but token present (grace window 3s) to avoid immediate 401 during redirects; (c) add e2e test for SSO POST+302 flows.

Sophie (eng-sre): I'll watch canary metrics and routes for errors (500/401 spike). If we see regressions we'll roll back the device-stamp rotation.

Maya (support): Action items: 1) Enable SameSite=None patch for this org on canary (Kevin) 2) Monitor for 2h (Sophie) 3) If stable, rollout to prod with migration notes (Maya to coordinate customer comms).

Kevin (eng-auth): I'll push the canary config change now and include telemetry to record cookie headers (trace id). Should have results in ~10m.

Eli (customer): Thanks — I see app loads fine in my tests when SameSite=None. Please let me know when you want me to verify in the live org. :thumbsup:

Sophie (eng-sre): saw initial canary runs — cookies now present on redirect for test flows. No error spike. Leaving monitoring on for 2h.

Kevin (eng-auth): Followup: created ticket AUTH-8421 to: track device-stamp rollback, TTL alignment, and e2e SSO tests. Assigning to eng-auth for the rollout.

Maya (support): Closing loop for now — will coordinate a scheduled patch and customer notice if canary stays green. Eli, we may ask you to test the window of ~30-60m after prod rollout.

Eli (customer): Happy to test. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

AuthBot: incident-tracker note: AUTH-8421 created and linked to canary deploy 2026-03-15T14:25:00Z

Kevin (eng-auth): TL;DR root cause = SameSite behavior + device_stamp rotation mismatch. Fix path = SameSite=None short-term + stop rotating device_stamp on initial SSO callback + align refresh token/cookie TTLs.

Maya (support): Tagging internal playbook: support/runbook/auth-session-sso.md with this incident for future reference. :memo:
